name: Wakefit Innovations Ltd
title: Wakefit Innovations Ltd - 544642 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Wakefit Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.6% YoY to Rs 404.9 cr; reported EBITDA margin 13.9% and gross margin 57.1%, with ~100 bps raw-material hit guided for H1.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 16.6% YoY to Rs 404.9 cr, with mattresses up 27.3% and about two-thirds of growth attributed to volume. Gross margin expanded to 57.1% (from 55.8%) and reported EBITDA rose 25.2% to Rs 56 cr (13.9% margin), while PAT rose 19.2% to Rs 23.3 cr but was hit by a Rs 7.3 cr deferred tax charge versus a Rs 98 cr deferred tax credit in Q4. Management flagged that polyol/TDI cost inflation from Middle East disruption will fully flow through in H1 FY27, and that furniture growth slowed due to deliberate pauses in furniture-first store openings.

financial_highlights.change: +19.2% YoY; includes Rs 7.3 cr deferred tax charge

segments.name: Mattress
segments.commentary: 65.9% of Q1 revenue, growing 27.3% YoY; about two-thirds volume and one-third price. Premium share of sales rose ~20-30% relative, but management says price hikes did not drive premiumisation.

segments.name: Furniture
segments.commentary: About 28% of revenue; growth slowed from ~30% last year due to machine breakdowns, workforce shortage, delivery-date backlog and a pause in furniture-first stores. Management guides mid-to-late teens growth over the next two quarters.

segments.name: Channels
segments.commentary: Own channels (COCO + D2C web/app) 72.3% of revenue, +20.5% YoY; external marketplaces/MBOs 27.7%, +7.6% YoY after two quarters of 15-20% decline.

guidance_outlook: Raw-material cost impact to fully reflect in H1 FY27; overall H1 gross margin compression of about 100-120 bps versus H1 last year, and about 100 bps lower than Q1 level (could be below 100 bps if prices stabilise).

Furniture category growth to return to mid-to-late teens over next two quarters; step-jump of more than 25-30% expected when Jumbo stores open (first Bangalore store targeted June-July 2027, second Aug-Sep 2027).
Add about 80 COCO stores in FY27 (27 added in Q1; 42 in all of FY26); similar number targeted next year.
FY27 capex of Rs 100-120 cr, ~80% for retail expansion (Jumbo stores), ~20% for manufacturing automation and upgrades.
Rental outgo for FY27 around Rs 80-90 cr; A&P at 7-8% of revenue for FY27; ESOP expense Rs 10-12 cr versus earlier Rs 12 cr guidance.
Long-term aspiration: operating EBITDA around 9% this year, steady state 2-3 years out; management seeks 20-25% revenue growth focus and 4-5 pp organised market share gain over 3-5 years.
capex_capacity: 165 COCO stores across 100 cities as of June 30, 2026 (about 105-106 mega stores with furniture; about 60 mini mattress-first stores).
MBO network about 2,250 outlets across 701 cities.
First Jumbo store: excavation nearly complete, civil work underway; second Jumbo store location under negotiation and approvals (both Bangalore).
Mini-store payback about 10-11 months; catchment revenue up ~2.7-3x after store opening; mini-store inventory about Rs 4-5 lakh.
Raw material buffer: about 3-4 weeks of inventory acquired at lower prices; blended cost still below spot.
demand_pricing: Raw-material spot prices rose 140-160% for some inputs and 70-80% for others; effective net inflation on acquisitions about 30-40%. Passed through via two price increases of about 5% each.

Price hikes first taken late March 2026; June began with a nominal price cut; July saw a modest further cut; management says prices broadly held since and no further hikes planned barring unforeseen increases.
Own channel growth 20.5% YoY; total online 52.7% of revenue, offline 47.3%; repeat customers about 36% of revenue; about two products per cart.
Organised mattress market share estimated at close to 10% (internal estimate, no industry report). B2B finished goods 2-3% of revenue.
Competitive intensity in mattresses described as stable; no new major entrants, with A&P raised from ~5% to ~7.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs value split of mattress growth and outlook for furniture growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds volume and one-third price for Q1; furniture to return to mid-to-late teens over next two quarters, with a step-up of 25-30% once Jumbo stores open. Full-year furniture growth not commented.

qa_highlights.question: Is further cost escalation expected and will more price hikes be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Conflict flares intermittently; supply shortages have pushed suppliers to higher prices. Management is monitoring weekly/monthly and says there is no visibility beyond a few weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin compression expected for H1 and why not pass through earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Full impact of costs bought in March-May lands in July-September. H1 margin compression about 100-120 bps; management says it absorbs short disruptions and adjusts price within 4-6 weeks of sustained moves.

qa_highlights.question: Own-channel versus marketplace growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Own channel up 20% YoY (website/app plus COCO); total online sales up 7% YoY. External channels recovered on platforms prioritising growth and a sale event, with a July sale also expected to help.

qa_highlights.question: Operating leverage, corporate overhead and EBITDA trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate overhead about 7-8% of revenue; absolute spend rising as senior hires join, but percentage expected to fall. Operating EBITDA about 9% this quarter, targeted near 7.5%-9% this year, with steady-state margins two to three years away.

qa_highlights.question: Store payback and expansion economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Mini-store payback around 10-11 months, about 2-3 months longer than mega stores; plan of at least 80 COCO stores this year and a similar number next year, with no guidance beyond that.

risks_watch: Raw-material volatility: polyol/TDI supply shortages and Middle East flare-ups; management has no visibility beyond a few weeks and reviews pricing weekly/monthly. Watch H1 gross margin compression of about 100-120 bps versus last year.
Inventory cushion is only about 3-4 weeks; once it is consumed, Q2 and Q3 gross margin depends on spot prices and the 4-6 week lag before price changes stick.

Furniture growth to return to mid-to-late teens over the next two quarters; full-year FY27 furniture growth not guided. Jumbo store go-live (Bangalore) targeted June-July 2027 and Aug-Sep 2027, so the step-up is outside FY27 for the first store.
ESOP expense guided at Rs 10-12 cr versus earlier Rs 12 cr, with senior hires expected in H2; corporate overhead (7-8% of revenue) may rise in absolute terms.
Store economics: mini-store payback about 10-11 months, still early for the ramp-up; 80 COCO store additions in FY27 and a similar number next year, with no guidance beyond that.
External marketplace channel growth (+7.6% YoY) rebounded from a 15-20% decline; sustainability depends on platform growth focus and sale events.
key_quotes: So, mattress has come back on track. It has always been our mainstay that enables us to build a flywheel.
But we have to wait and watch every few weeks.
When you look at the overall H1, it might not be more than 100 to 120 basis points unless something else happens in the rest of August and September in terms of driving up the prices.
Barring any unforeseen increases, we will not be touching the prices as of now.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the mattress franchise, with volume-led growth and a clear store rollout plan. Cautious and hedged on raw-material costs and H2 margins, repeatedly saying visibility is only a few weeks and that guidance depends on whether the Middle East conflict worsens.

adds.what: About 80 COCO stores in FY27 (27 added in Q1), incl. mega/mini stores
First Jumbo store in Bangalore (excavation nearly complete, civil work underway)
Second Jumbo store in Bangalore (location under negotiation and approvals), targeted Aug-Sep 2027

growth.why: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 16.6% YoY to Rs 404.9 cr, with about 80 COCO store additions and Rs 100-120 cr FY27 capex backing growth, and furniture guided back to mid-to-late teens; offset by ~100-120 bps H1 gross margin compression and the Jumbo stores only arriving in 2027.
